### HTML scraping

The goal of this analysis was to check whether including HTML headers in training data (2,165 webpages) improved binary class prediction accuracy. Webpages were either classified as having "No relevant content" or "Relevant claim content." We discovered that including header content does not improve prediction accuracy. After including headers, the Ridge regularized logistic principle component regression model accuracy decreased from 0.797 (baseline) to 0.771. Although these numbers are very similar, we can conclude that headers do not help prediction accuracy, so are not needed in the training data.  

### Bigrams

Bigrams do not appear to capture additional information helpful to the classification of whether or not a claim is or isn't relevant. We first extracted the important text from each of the claims, and turned each individual word into a single "token" or unigram. Based on these single words in each claim, we predicted whether or not the claim contained relevant content or not. We then repeated this process again this time using the two word phrases (bigrams) in each claim as well along with information about how strongly the individual words support one predicted class over another. As mentioned above, the baseline logistic regression model had a classification accuracy of 0.797. Interestingly enough, with the bigrams, the accuracy also dropped to 0.771, which could be due to the distortion of the stacked model. We reduced data complexity twice before stacking the models which may have created components with little discriminative power.

### Neural net

We trained a text-classification neural network using a standard Keras pipeline.

#### **Architecture**

The final model had the following structure:

-   **TextVectorization layer**\

    Converts raw text into integer sequences using a learned vocabulary of the top 10,000 tokens and a fixed sequence length of 100.

-   **Embedding layer**

    -   Vocabulary size: 10,001

    -   Embedding dimension: 16\
        Learns dense vector representations of tokens.

-   **GlobalAveragePooling1D layer**
    Aggregates token embeddings across the entire sequence into a single fixed-length vector, giving a compact sentence representation.

-   **Dense(16, ReLU) layer**
    Learns nonlinear combinations of the pooled embedding features.

-   **Dense(1, sigmoid) output layer**
    Produces a probability for the binary classification task.

#### **Optimization and Loss**

-   **Optimizer:** Adam

-   **Loss function:** Binary cross-entropy

-   **Evaluation metric:** Accuracy

    These choices are standard for binary text classification and typically yield fast, stable convergence.

    #### **Training Setup**

-   **Training epochs:** 5

-   **Batch size:** 32

-   **Data splits:**

    -   56% training

    -   24% validation

    -   20% held-out test set (never used during training or validation)

-   The TextVectorization layer was **adapted only on the training split** to avoid data leakage.

    #### **Predictive Accuracy**

    On the unseen test set, the model achieved:

    **Test accuracy: 0.7804**

    This exceeds the baseline logistic principal component regression accuracy (0.771–0.797 depending on preprocessing) and demonstrates that the neural network provides competitive or better predictive performance.
